findings.title: No drain window: health flip is unobservable before Shutdown closes the listener
findings.evidence: draining.Store(true) is immediately followed by srv.Shutdown(shutdownCtx); Shutdown closes listeners right away, so /healthz returns 503 only for requests already accepted, and any balancer that has not yet polled keeps sending traffic to a closed port.
findings.recommendation: Insert a configurable drain period (e.g. a 5s timer, still serving) between draining.Store(true) and srv.Shutdown, then give Shutdown the remaining budget; log the start/end of the drain so operators can tune it against the balancer poll interval.

findings.title: Graceful shutdown and forced-close paths have no test coverage
findings.evidence: The whole behaviour under review lives in main with a package-level atomic flag and no test file is added, so the SIGTERM handler, the 15s deadline and the forced Close path are unverified.
findings.recommendation: Extract the serve/shutdown logic into a testable function and add tests: signal during an in-flight request (request completes), request slower than the deadline (connection force-closed), and health returning 503 while draining.

findings.title: Forced close still exits with status 0
findings.evidence: After the deadline expires the code logs the failure and calls _ = srv.Close(), then falls out of main normally, so supervisors and alerting see a successful exit despite aborted in-flight requests.
findings.recommendation: Record that the shutdown was not graceful and exit non-zero (e.g. os.Exit(1) after logging) so a dropped-request shutdown is visible to orchestrators and metrics.
